news.text: In stock car racing, Kyle Larson wins the NASCAR Cup Series.

articles.title: 2026 NASCAR Cup Series
articles.extract: The 2026 NASCAR Cup Series was the 78th season for NASCAR professional stock car racing in the United States and the 55th season for the modern-era Cup Series. The preseason featured the Cook Out Clash exhibition race on February 4 at Bowman Gray Stadium, followed by the season-opening 68th running of the Daytona 500 on February 15 at Daytona International Speedway. The season ended at Homestead–Miami Speedway on November 8.

articles.title: Kyle Larson
articles.extract: Kyle Miyata Larson is an American professional racing driver. He competes full-time in the NASCAR Cup Series, driving the No. 5 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 for Hendrick Motorsports.

news.text: A mass shooting in the Main Square of Kraków, Poland, leaves six people dead and sixteen others injured.

articles.title: 2026 Kraków shooting
articles.extract: On 7 November 2026, a mass shooting took place in Kraków, Poland, when 24-year-old Michał Oksiński opened fire from his car as he drove through the Main Square, killing six people and injuring 16 others before being shot by police. Following the shooting, police discovered the dead bodies of three members of his family in their apartment in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski.

articles.title: Main Square, Kraków
articles.extract: The Main Market Square is a historic square in the Old Town of Kraków, Poland.

articles.title: Kraków
articles.extract: Kraków, officially the Royal Capital City of Kraków, is the second-largest and one of the oldest cities in Poland. Situated on the Vistula River in Lesser Poland Voivodeship, the city has a population of 816,614 (2025), with 1,428,363 people living in the Kraków metropolitan area. Kraków was the official capital of Poland until 1596 and has traditionally been one of the leading centres of Polish academic, cultural, and artistic life. Its Old Town was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978, one of the world's first sites granted the status.

news.text: President of Paraguay Santiago Peña is impeached, arrested, and replaced by Vice President Pedro Alliana amid a banking crisis involving Ueno Bank.

articles.title: 2026 Paraguay banking crisis
articles.extract: The 2026 Paraguay banking crisis is an ongoing financial and political crisis in Paraguay, triggered by the regulatory intervention and shutdown of Ueno Bank, the country's largest digital financial institution. The lender's collapse froze the liquid balances of approximately three million retail depositors, and endangered more than US$800 million in public and pension funds.

articles.title: Santiago Peña
articles.extract: Santiago Peña Palacios is a Paraguayan politician and economist who served as the 52nd president of Paraguay from 2023 until his arrest, dismissal, and prosecution in 2026. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay. He taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción.

articles.title: Pedro Alliana
articles.extract: Hércules Pedro Lorenzo Alliana Rodríguez is a Paraguayan politician serving as the president of Paraguay since 6 November 2026. A former national deputy from 2013 to 2023, he previously served as president of the Chamber of Deputies from 2019 to 2022, president of the Colorado Party from 2015 to 2023, and governor of Ñeembucú Department from 2008 to 2013. He succeeded Santiago Peña who was removed from office, arrested, and prosecuted in the wake of 2026 Paraguay banking crisis caused by the failure of Ueno Bank.

articles.title: Ueno Bank
articles.extract: Ueno Bank, legally Ueno Bank S.A., was a Paraguayan bank headquartered in Asunción. It operated primarily through digital payment platforms and originated from the consolidation of financial institutions with roots dating back to 1976. In November 2023, it obtained a banking license from the Central Bank of Paraguay, and in 2024 it absorbed Visión Banco, significantly expanding its customer base. By June 2026, it reported approximately 2.94 million customers, over 60% of Paraguay's adult population. The institution also maintained sponsorship agreements with major Paraguayan sporting organizations, including the Paraguayan Football Association, as well as cultural and social initiatives.

news.text: In the United States, the Democratic Party wins a majority in both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections.

articles.title: 2026 United States elections
articles.extract: Elections in the United States were held on November 3, 2026. In these midterm elections, which occurred during the non-consecutive second term of incumbent Republican president Donald Trump, all 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the U.S. Senate were contested to determine the 120th United States Congress. Thirty-nine state and territorial U.S. gubernatorial elections, attorney general elections, and numerous state and local elections were also contested. The Democratic Party obtained a majority in the Senate and House of Representatives, and among state governorships across the United States.

articles.title: Democratic Party (United States)
articles.extract: The Democratic Party is a liberal political party in the United States, sitting on the center to center-left of the political spectrum. Founded in 1828, it is the world's oldest active political party. Its main rival is the Republican Party, and since the 1850s, both have dominated American politics.

articles.title: United States House of Representatives
articles.extract: The United States House of Representatives is a chamber of the bicameral United States Congress; it is the lower house, with the United States Senate being the upper house. Together, the House and Senate have the authority under Article One of the Constitution of the United States in enumerated matters to pass or defeat federal legislation, known as bills. Those that are also passed by the Senate are sent to the president for signature or veto. The House's exclusive powers include initiating all revenue bills, impeaching federal officers, and electing the president if no candidate receives a majority of votes in the Electoral College.

articles.title: United States Senate
articles.extract: The United States Senate is a chamber of the bicameral United States Congress; it is the upper house, and the U.S. House of Representatives is the lower house. Together, the Senate and House have the authority under Article One of the Constitution to make and pass or defeat federal legislation.

news.text: In motorsport, Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest ever winner of the Formula One World Championship.

articles.title: 2026 Formula One World Championship
articles.extract: The 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship is a motor racing championship for Formula One cars and the 77th running of the Formula One World Championship. It is recognised by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the governing body of international motorsport, as the highest class of competition for open-wheel racing cars. The championship is contested over twenty-three Grands Prix held around the world. It began in March and is scheduled to end in December. Drivers and teams compete for the titles of World Drivers' Champion and World Constructors' Champion, respectively. Lando Norris was the reigning World Drivers' Champion, while McLaren-Mercedes are the reigning World Constructors' Champions. The World Drivers' Championship was clinched by Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli at the Mexico City Grand Prix. It was his maiden title in his second year competing in Formula One, becoming the youngest ever champion in Formula One history and the first Italian to win the championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Mercedes secured their ninth Constructors' Championship at the São Paulo Grand Prix.

articles.title: Motorsport
articles.extract: Motorsport are sporting events, competitions and related activities that primarily involve the use of automobiles, motorcycles, motorboats and powered aircraft. For each of these vehicle types, the more specific terms automobile sport, motorcycle sport, power boating and air sports may be used commonly, or officially by organisers and governing bodies.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli
articles.extract: Andrea Kimi Antonelli is an Italian racing driver who competes in Formula One for Mercedes. Antonelli won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2026 with Mercedes, becoming the youngest-ever World Drivers' Champion; he has won nine Grands Prix since his debut in 2025.

mostRead.title: Ramayana: Part 1
mostRead.extract: Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the Hindu epic Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first of a two-part film, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana which chronicles the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The first part features ensemble cast that includes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta.

mostRead.title: Russell Brand
mostRead.extract: Russell Edward Brand is an English comedian, actor and media personality. He rose to prominence as a reality television presenter in the early 2000s before starring in major comedy films, releasing several stand-up specials and hosting radio shows. In 2026, he was convicted of rape and sexual assault, and sentenced to ten years and six months in prison.

mostRead.title: Jensen Huang
mostRead.extract: Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang is a Taiwanese and American electrical engineer and business executive who is the co-founder, president, and CEO of Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies. As of October 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at over US$200 billion, making him the seventh-wealthiest individual in the world.

mostRead.title: David Walliams
mostRead.extract: David Edward Williams, known professionally as David Walliams, is an English actor, comedian, writer and television personality. He rose to prominence for his work with Matt Lucas on the BBC sketch comedy series Little Britain (2003–2006) and Come Fly with Me (2010–2011). From 2012 to 2022, Walliams was a judge on the television talent competition Britain's Got Talent, for which he received multiple National Television Awards.

mostRead.title: Thomas Massie
mostRead.extract: Thomas Harold Massie is an American politician. A member of the Republican Party, Massie has been the United States representative for Kentucky's 4th congressional district since 2012.

mostRead.title: SS Edmund Fitzgerald
mostRead.extract: SS Edmund Fitzgerald was an American Great Lakes freighter that sank in Lake Superior during a storm on November 10, 1975, with the loss of the entire crew of 29 men. When launched on June 7, 1958, she was the largest ship on North America's Great Lakes and remains the largest to have sunk there. Her wreck was located in deep water on November 14, 1975, by a U.S. Navy aircraft detecting magnetic anomalies, and soon afterwards found to be in two large pieces.

mostRead.title: Carson Wentz
mostRead.extract: Carson James Wentz is an American professional football quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football for the North Dakota State Bison, winning two consecutive NCAA FCS national championships between 2014 and 2015. Wentz was selected second overall by the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2016 NFL draft, making him the highest drafted FCS player.

mostRead.title: Scene (2026 film)
mostRead.extract: Scene is a 2026 Indian Tamil-language action comedy film written and directed by Jithu Madhavan. Produced by Suriya and Jyothika's 2D Entertainment and the newly established Zhagaram Studios, the film stars Suriya, Naslen and Nazriya Nazim, with Anandaraj, Lal, Rajpriyan, Suresh Mathiyalagan and Gajaraj in supporting roles. It revolves around a DSP being forced to reopen an unfinished case and solve it with a troublesome team.

mostRead.title: Lara Stone
mostRead.extract: Lara Catherina Stone is a Dutch model. She was discovered at the age of 12 in the Paris Metro and later participated in the Elite Model Look competition at 15. Stone has appeared on the covers of W and Vogue, has worked with various brands, including Fendi, Chanel, Prada, Louis Vuitton, and Versace, and was most notably the face of Calvin Klein. She has been represented by The Lions, IMG Models, and Elite Model Management.

mostRead.title: Deaths in 2026
mostRead.extract: The following notable deaths occurred in 2026. Names are reported under the date of death, in alphabetical order. A typical entry reports information in the following sequence:Name, age, country of citizenship at birth, subsequent nationality, what subject was noted for, cause of death, and a reference.

mostRead.title: Kirk Cousins
mostRead.extract: Kirk Daniel Cousins is an American professional football quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football for the Michigan State Spartans and was selected by the Washington Redskins in the fourth round of the 2012 NFL draft.

mostRead.title: Pete Hegseth
mostRead.extract: Peter Brian Hegseth is an American politician, U.S. Army veteran, and former television personality who has been serving as the 29th United States secretary of defense since 2025.

mostRead.title: Nvidia
mostRead.extract: Nvidia Corporation is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company develops graphics processing units (GPUs), systems on chips (SoCs), and application programming interfaces (APIs) for data science, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence (AI) hardware, and mobile and automotive applications. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia has been described as a Big Tech company and is among the largest companies by market capitalization.

mostRead.title: List of highest-grossing Indian films
mostRead.extract: This ranking lists the highest-grossing Indian films produced by Indian cinema, based on conservative global box office estimates as reported by organisations classified as green by Wikipedia. The figures are not adjusted for inflation. However, there is no official tracking of figures and sources publishing data are frequently pressured to increase their estimates.

mostRead.title: Abdul El-Sayed
mostRead.extract: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed is an American politician, epidemiologist, and academic who is the United States Senator-elect from Michigan.

mostRead.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
mostRead.extract: Godzilla Minus Zero  is a 2026 Japanese epic kaiju film written, directed, and with visual effects by Takashi Yamazaki. A sequel to Godzilla Minus One (2023), it is the 39th film in the Godzilla franchise, the 34th film thereof produced by Toho, and the sixth installment in the Reiwa era. The film stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Yuki Yamada, Kuranosuke Sasaki, Sakura Ando, and Miou Tanaka reprising their roles from Minus One, with Min Tanaka, Masami Nagasawa, and Jun Kunimura also starring as new characters. In the film, set in 1949, postwar Japan struggles to rebuild when it faces a new threat: King Ghidorah. Godzilla reappears and is drawn into conflict with the three-headed monster, guided through human intervention.

mostRead.title: Jemima Goldsmith
mostRead.extract: Jemima Marcelle Goldsmith O'Reilly, formerly known professionally as Jemima Khan, is an English TV and film producer and screenwriter. She is the founder of Instinct Productions, a television production company. Previously she was an associate editor for the British political and cultural magazine The New Statesman and European editor-at-large for the American magazine Vanity Fair.

mostRead.title: Survivor Series: WarGames (2026)
mostRead.extract: The 2026 Survivor Series: WarGames, also promoted as Survivor Series: WarGames Houston, is an upcoming professional wrestling premium live event (PLE) produced by WWE, to be held for wrestlers from the promotion's main roster brands, Raw and SmackDown as well as their partner promotion Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide. It will be the 40th annual Survivor Series, and the fifth annual branded as "WarGames", and it will take place during Thanksgiving weekend on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at Daikin Park in Houston, Texas and the second Survivor Series overall in the city since 2017.

mostRead.title: 2026 United States elections
mostRead.extract: Elections in the United States were held on November 3, 2026. In these midterm elections, which occurred during the non-consecutive second term of incumbent Republican president Donald Trump, all 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the U.S. Senate were contested to determine the 120th United States Congress. Thirty-nine state and territorial U.S. gubernatorial elections, attorney general elections, and numerous state and local elections were also contested. The Democratic Party obtained a majority in the Senate and House of Representatives, and among state governorships across the United States.

mostRead.title: Adrian Peterson
mostRead.extract: Adrian Lewis Peterson is an American former professional football running back. Peterson played 15 seasons in the National Football League (NFL). He is widely considered to be one of the greatest running backs in football history. He played college football for the Oklahoma Sooners, setting the freshman rushing record with 1,925 yards in 2004. Named a unanimous All-American that year, he became the first freshman to finish as a runner-up in the Heisman Trophy balloting. Peterson finished his college career as the Sooners' third-all-time leading rusher.

mostRead.title: The End of Everything (Harrison novel)
mostRead.extract: The End of Everything is a 2026 post-apocalyptic novel by M. John Harrison, published in the UK by Serpent's Tail. It is Harrison's 13th novel and won the 2026 Booker Prize.

mostRead.title: Jailer 2
mostRead.extract: Jailer 2 is a 2026 Indian Tamil-language action comedy film written and directed by Nelson Dilipkumar. It was produced by Kalanithi Maran through Sun Pictures. A sequel to Jailer (2023), the film stars Rajinikanth, Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa and Rithvik reprising their roles from the predecessor, with S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu and Vidya Balan joining the cast.

mostRead.title: Lauren Boebert
mostRead.extract: Lauren Opal Boebert is an American politician, businesswoman, and gun rights activist serving as the U.S. representative for Colorado's 4th congressional district beginning in 2025, having previously represented Colorado's 3rd congressional district from 2021 to 2025. From 2013 to 2022, she owned Shooters Grill, a restaurant in Rifle, Colorado, where staff members were encouraged to carry firearms openly.

mostRead.title: Elizabeth Holmes
mostRead.extract: Elizabeth Anne Holmes is an American businesswoman convicted of fraud in connection with her health technology company Theranos. Holmes founded Theranos in 2003, and its valuation soared in the early 2010s after it claimed to have revolutionized blood testing by developing methods that needed only very small volumes of blood, such as from a fingerprick. In 2015, Forbes named Holmes the youngest and wealthiest self-made female billionaire in the United States on the basis of a $9 billion valuation of Theranos. In the following year, as accusations of fraud about Theranos's claims began to surface, Forbes revised its estimate of Holmes's net worth to zero, and Fortune named her in its feature article on "The World's 19 Most Disappointing Leaders".

mostRead.title: Ansel Adams
mostRead.extract: Ansel Easton Adams was an American landscape photographer and environmentalist known for his black-and-white images of the American West. He helped found Group f/64, an association of photographers advocating "pure" photography which favored sharp focus and the use of the full tonal range of a photograph. He and Fred Archer developed a system of image-making called the Zone System, a method of achieving a desired final print through a technical understanding of how the tonal range of an image is the result of choices made in exposure, negative development, and printing.

mostRead.title: Stephen Miller
mostRead.extract: Stephen N. Miller is an American political advisor who has served as the White House chief of staff since 2026. Miller has additionally served as the homeland security advisor since 2025. He previously served as the White House deputy chief of staff for policy from 2025 to 2026, and as the senior advisor to the president and the White House director of speechwriting from 2017 to 2021. Considered one of the most influential figures of the Trump administrations and Trumpism movement, Miller's politics have been described as far-right, ultraconservative, anti-immigrant, ultranationalist, and white nationalist.

mostRead.title: Pawan Kalyan
mostRead.extract: Konidela Pawan Kalyan is an Indian politician, actor, philanthropist, and martial artist serving as the 11th Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh since June 2024. He also serves as the Minister for Panchayat Raj, Rural Development and Rural Water Supply; Environment, Forest, Science and Technology in the Government of Andhra Pradesh as MLA representing the Pithapuram constituency. He is the founder and president of the Janasena Party.

mostRead.title: Mauricio Pochettino
mostRead.extract: Mauricio Roberto Pochettino Trossero is an Argentine professional football manager and former footballer who is the head coach of the United States men's national team.

mostRead.title: Toukie Smith
mostRead.extract: Doris A. Smith, known professionally as Toukie Smith, was an American actress and model. She was best known for her role as Eva Rawley on the NBC sitcom 227 (1989–90). She was the sister of fashion designer Willi Smith.

mostRead.title: VisionQuest
mostRead.extract: VisionQuest is an American television miniseries created by Terry Matalas for the streaming service Disney+, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Vision. A spin-off from and sequel to the miniseries WandaVision (2021), it is the 18th television series in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) from Marvel Studios and is produced under its Marvel Television label. The series shares continuity with the films of the MCU. It follows the synthezoid Vision as he attempts to understand who he is by communicating with AI personas embedded in his programming, and goes on the run with a mysterious teenager who may be his reincarnated son. Matalas serves as showrunner and a director.

mostRead.title: Joran van der Sloot
mostRead.extract: Joran Andreas Petrus van der Sloot is a Dutch murderer, extortionist, con man, and drug trafficker who was convicted in the 2010 killing of Stephany Flores Ramírez in Lima, Peru. He first came to public attention as the prime suspect in the disappearance of Natalee Holloway in 2005.

mostRead.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
mostRead.extract: Grand Theft Auto VI is an upcoming action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games. It is due to be the eighth main entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V, and the sixteenth entry overall. Set within the fictional US state of Leonida, based on Florida, the story follows the criminal duo of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Players will be able to freely roam Leonida's open world, which features the Miami-inspired Vice City.

mostRead.title: Lisa Su
mostRead.extract: Lisa Tzwu-Fang Su is a Taiwanese and American business executive, computer scientist, and electrical engineer who has been the president and CEO of the American semiconductor company AMD since 2014.

mostRead.title: Katy Perry
mostRead.extract: Katheryn Elizabeth Hudson, known professionally as Katy Perry, is an American singer, songwriter, and television personality. Known for her influence on pop music and her camp style, she has been dubbed the "Queen of Camp" by Vogue and Rolling Stone.

mostRead.title: Jim Jordan
mostRead.extract: James Daniel Jordan is an American politician who has served in the U.S. House of Representatives as the representative for Ohio's 4th congressional district since 2007. Currently in his 10th term in the House, Jordan is a member of the Republican Party. He was chosen on November 10, 2026, to serve as the Republican House Minority Leader in the 120th Congress.

mostRead.title: Clayface (film)
mostRead.extract: Clayface is a 2026 American body horror film based on the eponymous character from DC Comics. Directed by James Watkins from a screenplay by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, it is the third film in the DC Universe (DCU). Tom Rhys Harries stars as Matt Hagen / Clayface, alongside Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella, and Eddie Marsan. In the film, after becoming disfigured by a mobster (Dencik), rising actor Matt Hagen seeks help from a scientist (Ackie) to restore his appearance, but the procedure transforms him into a shapeshifting creature. It is produced by Matt Reeves and Lynn Harris alongside James Gunn and Peter Safran of DC Studios.

mostRead.title: Black Doves
mostRead.extract: Black Doves is a British spy action thriller television series created by Joe Barton. The series, starring Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, and Sarah Lancashire, is developed by Sister and Barton's production company Noisy Bear for Netflix. The series is about a spies-for-hire organisation that obtains secrets for the highest bidder. Ahead of its premiere on 5 December 2024, it was renewed for a second series which was released in full on 5 November 2026.

mostRead.title: Josh Allen
mostRead.extract: Joshua Patrick Allen is an American professional football quarterback for the Buffalo Bills of the National Football League (NFL). A lightly recruited high school prospect, Allen began his college football career with the Reedley Tigers before transferring to the Wyoming Cowboys. He was selected seventh overall by the Bills in the 2018 NFL draft.

mostRead.title: 2026 Kraków shooting
mostRead.extract: On 7 November 2026, a mass shooting took place in Kraków, Poland, when 24-year-old Michał Oksiński opened fire from his car as he drove through the Main Square, killing six people and injuring 16 others before being shot by police. Following the shooting, police discovered the dead bodies of three members of his family in their apartment in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski.

mostRead.title: You Can See Everything
mostRead.extract: You Can See Everything is a 2026 American documentary film directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. It follows Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of the defunct health technology company Theranos, and her partner Billy Evans, who invited a film crew to document them beginning in the weeks before Holmes began serving a United States federal prison sentence for defrauding investors.

mostRead.title: Jon Ossoff
mostRead.extract: Thomas Jonathan Ossoff is an American politician who has served since 2021 as the senior United States senator from Georgia. A member of the Democratic Party, he is the youngest incumbent U.S. senator.

mostRead.title: James Talarico
mostRead.extract: James Dell Talarico is an American politician and educator who is the United States senator-elect from Texas. A member of the Democratic Party, he has served since 2018 as a member of the Texas House of Representatives.

mostRead.title: M. John Harrison
mostRead.extract: Michael John Harrison, known for publication purposes primarily as M. John Harrison, is an English author and literary critic. His work includes the Viriconium sequence of novels and short stories (1971–1984), Climbers (1989), and the Kefahuchi Tract trilogy, which consists of Light (2002), Nova Swing (2006) and Empty Space (2012). His novel The End of Everything won the Booker Prize in 2026.

featuredArticle.title: U.S. Route 101
featuredArticle.extract: U.S. Route 101, or U.S. Highway 101 (US 101), is a major north–south highway that traverses the states of California, Oregon, and Washington on the West Coast of the United States. It is part of the United States Numbered Highway System and runs for over 1,500 miles (2,400 km) along the Pacific Ocean. The highway is also known by various names, including El Camino Real in parts of California, the Oregon Coast Highway, and the Olympic Highway in Washington. Despite its three-digit number, normally used for spur routes, US 101 is classified as a primary route with 10 as its "first digit".

events.text: A vehicle-ramming attack in Zhuhai, China, kills 38 people and injures 48.
Russo-Ukrainian War: Ukrainian armed forces enter the city of Kherson following a successful two-month southern counteroffensive.
Typhoon Vamco makes landfall in Luzon and several offshore islands, killing 67 people. The storm causes the worst floods in the region since Typhoon Ketsana in 2009.
A strong earthquake with the magnitude 6.8 hits northern Burma, killing at least 26 people.
A helicopter crash just outside Mexico City kills seven, including Francisco Blake Mora the Secretary of the Interior of Mexico.
After 30 years in power, Maumoon Abdul Gayoom was succeeded by Mohamed Nasheed as the president of the Maldives.
Queen Elizabeth II unveils the New Zealand War Memorial in London, United Kingdom, commemorating the loss of soldiers from the New Zealand Army and the British Army.
New Zealand Tomb of the Unknown Warrior is dedicated at the National War Memorial, Wellington.
The Palestine Liberation Organization confirms the death of Yasser Arafat from unidentified causes. Mahmoud Abbas is elected chairman of the PLO minutes later.
A Fokker F27 Friendship operating as Laoag International Airlines Flight 585 crashes into Manila Bay shortly after takeoff from Ninoy Aquino International Airport, killing 19 people.

Russian mathematician Grigori Perelman posts the first of three preprint texts with his proof of the Poincaré conjecture. It remains the only of the Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics to be solved. He later refused both the prize money from Clay Mathematics Institute as well as the Fields Medal for his work.
Journalists Pierre Billaud, Johanne Sutton and Volker Handloik are killed in Afghanistan during an attack on the convoy they are traveling in.
Kaprun disaster: One hundred fifty-five skiers and snowboarders die when a cable car catches fire in an alpine tunnel in Kaprun, Austria.
The House of Lords Act is given Royal Assent, restricting membership of the British House of Lords by virtue of a hereditary peerage.
A sculpture honoring women who served in the Vietnam War is dedicated at the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C.
The General Synod of the Church of England votes to allow women to become priests.
Space Shuttle Columbia launches from the Kennedy Space Center on STS-5, the first operational mission of the Space Shuttle program.
Antigua and Barbuda joins the United Nations.
A munitions explosion at a train station in Iri, South Korea kills at least 56 people.

Australian constitutional crisis of 1975: Australian Governor-General Sir John Kerr dismisses the government of Gough Whitlam, appoints Malcolm Fraser as caretaker Prime Minister and announces a general election to be held in early December.
Independence of Angola.
Vietnam War: Vietnamization: The United States Army turns over the massive Long Binh military base to South Vietnam.
Vietnam War: Operation Commando Hunt initiated. The goal is to interdict men and supplies on the Ho Chi Minh trail, through Laos into South Vietnam.
Vietnam War: In a propaganda ceremony in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, three American prisoners of war are released by the Viet Cong and turned over to "new left" antiwar activist Tom Hayden.
NASA launches Gemini 12.
Southern Rhodesia's Prime Minister Ian Smith unilaterally declares the colony independent as the unrecognised state of Rhodesia.
United Air Lines Flight 227 crashes at Salt Lake City International Airport, killing 43.
Kuwait's National Assembly ratifies the Constitution of Kuwait.
Thirteen Italian Air Force servicemen, deployed to the Congo as a part of the UN peacekeeping force, are massacred by a mob in Kindu.
A military coup against President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam is crushed.
The People's Liberation Army Air Force is founded.
World War II: France's zone libre is occupied by German forces in Case Anton.

The Turkish parliament passes the Varlık Vergisi, a capital tax mostly levied on non-Muslim citizens with the unofficial aim to inflict financial ruin on them and end their prominence in the country's economy.
World War II: In the Battle of Taranto, the Royal Navy launches the first all-aircraft ship-to-ship naval attack in history.
World War II: The German auxiliary cruiser Atlantis captures top secret British mail from the Automedon, and sends it to Japan.
The Shrine of Remembrance is opened in Melbourne, Australia.
Patent number US1781541 is awarded to Albert Einstein and Leó Szilárd for their invention, the Einstein refrigerator.
The United States Numbered Highway System is established.
Adolf Hitler is arrested in Munich for high treason for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch.
The Tomb of the Unknowns is dedicated by U.S. President Warren G. Harding at Arlington National Cemetery.
